structured_output.what_is_happening: NPC (97bgrx…) is a copy of the real "NPCs" $NPC token (@wenpcfamily, wenpc.family). The real project is an "AI NPC wallets spawned from creator fees" meme. It launched on pump.fun, and the likely canonical contract is 68SVgJ…pump, worth about $6.76M, up about 14,000% in 24h, with $232k liquidity. This copy was minted and paired straight on PumpSwap about 3 seconds after creation (created_unix 1790231829, pool 1790231832). It has no pump.fun launchpad or migration and no "pump" address suffix. It is about 50 minutes old, up about 900% to roughly $99k mcap, and has about 1,943 unique buyers. Most of that flow likely comes from buyers and bots confusing it with the canonical coin. The packet lists at least 7 other same-name "NPCs" tokens from the last few hours that now have $0 liquidity. Three of them (a4h4kL…, JBVpRS…, GQZMks…) also have no pump suffix, the same off-launchpad pattern as this one. Those look like copycats that were already rugged. The creator holds 18.59%, the LP is 0% locked/burned, and RugCheck flags 'Large Amount of LP Unlocked', 'Low amount of LP Providers' and 'Copycat token'.

narrative.description: The story: autonomous AI 'NPC' wallets that are funded by pump.fun creator fees, buy $NPC and trade other pump.fun coins. It builds on the well-known NPC/Wojak meme. The narrative is live today, and the canonical token has grown from zero to about $6.8M in a few hours.
narrative.why_spreading: The canonical $NPC ran about 140x today, which pulls in copycat deployers and confused buyers searching the ticker. This copy is taking spillover attention, not attention of its own.

token_connection.why_this_token: None beyond the copied name and ticker. The project site says it launched on pump.fun, but this contract was deployed off-launchpad straight to PumpSwap. The @wenpcfamily handle on GeckoTerminal is most likely copied metadata.
token_connection.competing_tokens: 68SVgJMajJ7YvW8fMU23jdwxCkCoFmVKdKcLMQ8qpump ($6.76M, likely canonical). At least 7 dead same-name copies with $0 liquidity. There are also older unrelated NPC tickers (Non-Playable Coin, $86-189M).

authenticity.evidence: GMGN shows a zero bot/degen rate and no snipers or bundlers. On the other hand, the contract was deployed off-launchpad with an unlocked, single-provider LP; the creator holds 18.6%; and RugCheck flags it as a copycat. Several same-name copies from today already have $0 liquidity. The 1,943 buyers look like ticker-confusion flow, not attention for this contract. I found no posts mentioning this contract address.
authenticity.uncertainty: I can't see who holds the LP or whether the creator is linked to the earlier dead copies. The dev address is new (1 launched token), with no funding source.

structural_risks: The LP is 0% locked/burned and has few providers, so the deployer can pull liquidity at any time
The creator holds 18.59% of supply and can dump it into the $64k pool
It is a copycat of a $6.8M canonical token, and several same-pattern copies from today are already at $0 liquidity
The buy flow is likely confused buyers who may leave once they realise it is the wrong contract

structured_output.counterargument: About 1,950 holders, $360k volume in an hour and a 3:1 buy/sell ratio is real demand. GMGN shows no snipers, bundlers or bots. The canonical narrative is hot, and a $100k copy of a $6.8M coin can move 2x on confusion flow alone. If the deployer is patient and farms fees or sells slowly instead of pulling the LP, the price could double first.
